content.title: About
content.content: An egg sandwich on an English muffin consists of a freshly cooked egg (fried, scrambled, boiled or poached) placed between a split English muffin, often topped with cheese, ham, avocado or greens. It is a quick, nutritious breakfast popular in cafés and fast‑food chains.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The English muffin originated in the United States in the early 20th century and was originally called an "English muffin".
Eggs are one of the most affordable sources of complete protein.
The sandwich can be made with any egg doneness—from soft poached to fully fried.
Variations with cheddar or Swiss cheese are often served with melted cheese for a crispy top.
The recipe is easily adaptable for dietary needs: whole‑grain muffins, added vegetables, or tofu scramble can replace the egg.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Eggs provide all essential amino acids, supporting muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs contain B2, B6, B12 which aid energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Source of vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D in eggs helps maintain bone health and immune function.

items.title: Moderate carbohydrate content
items.content: The English muffin supplies complex carbs, making the sandwich suitable for moderate low‑carb diets.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The combination of protein and carbs keeps you feeling full longer.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to eggs, ranging from mild to severe anaphylaxis.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Egg yolks contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should monitor egg intake.

items.title: Sodium in processed muffins
items.content: Store‑bought English muffins often contain added salt; choose low‑sodium versions if you have hypertension.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Undercooked eggs may harbor Salmonella; ensure eggs are fully cooked if safety is a concern.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the sandwich hot by splitting the muffin, placing the egg between the halves, and adding cheese, ham, avocado, tomato or leafy greens as desired. For a lighter version, use a whole‑grain muffin and cook the egg without added fat.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The sandwich is best eaten immediately. If needed, wrap tightly in foil or plastic wrap and refrigerate for up to 24 hours. Muffins store in a dry, airtight container for up to 5 days.
